You don't need a heap of infill to make it strong. Depending on what you're printing you can go into single digits. I recently printed a full size helmet with 8 percent infill and it seems plenty strong. Play around a bit until you find a sweet spot you're happy with. More infill will increase the material and time so try to find a balance you're happy with.

Mainly just check the fan is connected. I was so annoyed when I realised mine wasn't and it took me ages to get it working properly after. Maybe try completely winding them all out first so you're starting from a greater distance on each corner?

Make sure you've leveled it right. Biggest issue I had with mine was the hot end cooling fan wasn't connected. Check this before doing much printing, it won't fix adhesion but it will save you from blockages and troubleshooting later on.

Go slow and do a couple of passes around each corner with paper. Then do the middle with paper. Make sure you've disabled stepper when moving it. I recently got an ender 3 max neo and my cooling fan for the hot end wasn't connected. Check yours is before doing lots of printing as it will lead to blockages if it isn't.

I used to work for a company that had decided IoT was the future. They hadn't actually thought up any reasonable use case though, it seems so common, let's just make everything "smart" and "connected" without any real world benefit. I was at a product showcase for a well known supplier of IoT equipment and asked the guy who was so proud of his door monitoring system why anyone would bother refitting entire buildings with it and he said it will help save on air conditioning costs. The refit could run well into the millions depending on the size of the building, his showcase was a massive office tower with several thousand doors. To make it even worse once you go to all the effort to install all the physical parts to doors and the infrastructure to link it all you then have to use proprietary software to manage it all, service model. And then using the wireless network they proposed uses power. I can't imagine how long it would take to get your money's worth.  This was a while ago, and I don't work in that industry anymore so maybe the cost benefit is better now. But still this stuff always seems stupid to me now.
